If the call would only pass information one way, send an email (or a short recorded walkthrough) instead. Deals close over email all the time, so a call is never a required step. rules.title: A minute or two of small talk, then state the goal
rules.rule: Open with one or two minutes of light small talk that doesn't pry: where they are, how things are going, something public about their work. Then state the goal of the call and what you hope to agree by the end. Every question after that ties back to the goal; if the talk drifts, bring it back. Ask questions conversationally, not as an interrogation, and invite theirs.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: Have a one to two minute little chat with a person. Ask how the weather is. Ask how he's been doing. Ask about a specific thing you heard about him. Ask about where his name is from. A little thing. Break the ice. Don't be weird. Don't ask super intrusive questions.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: To take control of the call and state what the goal of the call is and what you're going to speak about and what you want from it.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: Make sure you don't sound pushy like an interrogation or question, question, question.

rules.title: Leave with a next step, then confirm it by email
rules.rule: Before the call ends, ask what the next steps are and agree on them out loud: a next meeting, a document they will send, a decision by a date. After the call, send a short email: thanks, a quick summary, anything promised (a file, the recording), and the agreed next step with its date. If a call ends with no next step, it should have been an email.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: So what's the next step? Okay, so what are the action steps from now?

src.quote: hey, was lovely speaking to you. Here's a quick summary. You can send them a meeting recording. Or hey, lovely meeting you. Here's the file you asked for. Looking forward to our chat on Friday.

rules.title: Selling on a call: understand first, then the plan, then the price
rules.rule: A call that sells runs in this order: small talk and the goal, then discovery (their situation, agencies and brands they have worked with, what they want), then agreeing together on the one main problem, then showing how we would solve it with concrete first steps, and only then the price or commission. Before naming the price, check that the plan really solves their problem. Answer concerns heard in discovery (for example 'agencies charge too much') before the price comes up, not after it.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: the price is the last thing you do, or the percentage you charge is the last thing

rules.title: Discovery finds their real problem; it never inflates one
rules.rule: Pitch only against the biggest problem they actually have, confirmed in their own words. If their real problem is something we don't solve, don't stretch our offer to fit it. The course teaches pressing on a small creator's pain before the pitch. House reading, ethics first: ask in order to understand, then reflect back what they said. Never exaggerate the problem, invent urgency, or keep pressing after they say it isn't a problem (FND-ETH-10). Every example in a pitch must be real: name past clients, results or brands we have only when it is true.
dont: Paint their situation worse than they described it
Use 'that's how we helped X' or 'we already have brands like Y' unless it is true

Trying to identify the biggest issue that he has, the biggest problem that he has.

rules.title: Brands buy on trust and numbers
rules.rule: Brands, and big creators with staff and bills, decide on logic: whether we look legitimate (how we carry ourselves, case studies) and whether the numbers make sense, meaning the return against what they spend. A return of three to ten times is a strong case. Don't probe a brand's pain points emotionally. A small creator decides more personally, so talk about what steady deals would change for them (more time for videos, paying their editor), using their own words.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: if you're selling to a business, let's say you're selling to a brand, which is a huge company, don't even try and squeeze on the pain or squeeze on the pain points.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls
src.quote: They need the numbers to make sense. That's it. They basically, and the simple way to think about it is they need to be making more than what they spend. And three to ten times more is a great number in terms of return on investment.

rules.title: Tailored offers take two calls, and the decision maker hears the pitch
rules.rule: When the offer has to be built for them (a brand campaign, a big creator), end the first call after discovery: say we'll prepare an offer and get back to them, and book the next call. Present the offer to the person who decides, on the second call or by email. If the first call was with someone who can't decide, ask them to bring the decision maker and send that person a summary before the call. A flat commission for a creator needs no second call.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

You can also just send him an email with the offer. I usually prefer to do it on the call.

rules.title: Nothing is signed or paid on a call
rules.rule: Never take a payment or sign a contract during a call. Send the contract or the invoice by email afterwards, and give them time to read it and bring in whoever else decides. Pushing for a commitment on the same call looks wrong.

src.doc: video:module 8 Bonuses/8.How To Take sales calls

rules.title: Record calls openly
rules.rule: Record every call with a note-taker that joins the call visibly, and tell the other side at the start that it is recorded (house reading, ethics first: never record in secret). The recording settles any later disagreement over what was said, and its summary feeds the recap email (FND-CALL-06).

rules.title: Two people per brand domain per day, at most
rules.rule: When writing to several people at one brand, email at most two of them on the same day, and add the next two the following day alongside the follow-ups. Each email is written for its reader (FND-WRITE-03). Mailbox providers now flag a burst of emails to one domain.

rules.title: Sell like a marketer, not a broker
rules.rule: Brands work through an agency, instead of going to the creator directly, when the agency brings expertise: why this creator's audience matches their buyers, which video the ad belongs in, how the creator should present the product, what happens if it underperforms, and the return on their spend. Pitches and replies show that thinking. An agency that only passes a creator along is a commodity, and brands go around it.

rules.rule: Answering quickly is not needy; neediness is in the tone (FND-MIND-03). Reply while they are still in their inbox and interested. do: Answer the question first, in the first line or two
Keep a reply to a one-line message to about three short sentences plus the ask
dont: Explain how the agency works when nobody asked
Reassure them about things they did not raise (that they are free to work with other agencies, that they can say no)
Add a disclaimer about what has not happened yet; the right verb already says it (INF-FIRST-21)
Describe a brand they can look up in a word, or tell a creator who a brand sponsored
List several of their own videos back to them
Apologise or justify at length

rules.title: No religious phrases in business messages, and a plain greeting in cold ones
rules.rule: Phrases like 'inshallah' or 'keep it halal' stay out of messages to creators and brands who may not share our faith: they confuse or put people off. A cold first message opens with a plain 'Hi' or 'Hey' even to someone who shares it: from a stranger, a religious greeting can read as using faith to get closer. Once the conversation is warm, follow their lead. The agency's halal principles are applied in what we choose to do (FND-ETH), not announced in the wording. This is the default of house choice HC-32; the alternative is FND-WRITE-29.
